You're working in the git worktree /opt/nxeon-wip-discord-bridge (branch feature/discord-support-bridge, already created off latest main in /opt/nxeon, node_modules and .env symlinked from /opt/nxeon — this means you have access to REAL, LIVE Discord credentials and a REAL Discord server, described below). Do NOT touch /opt/nxeon directly, do NOT merge or deploy — make the changes, verify, and report back. Do NOT run `git add -A` (a documented past incident replaced prod's real node_modules with a self-referential symlink) — stage specific files by name only if asked to commit (only commit if explicitly asked; leave it uncommitted otherwise).

## Context: what you're building and why

Nxeon (a VPS/hosting/game-server platform) wants a Discord bridge for its support system. This was already the subject of a deep, thorough research pass this session (codebase audit + sourced Discord-platform research) which produced a concrete architecture. You are now EXECUTING that plan, not re-researching it — the plan below is the ground truth, already vetted.

**Scope for THIS build, explicitly narrowed by the owner**: this is for the owner's OWN PERSONAL USE right now (not a team of support staff yet — that's a future phase). The stated goal: get push notifications on their phone when a customer opens a ticket or live chat, and be able to reply from Discord and have it actually reach the customer through Nxeon's real system. Build Phase 1 (mirror) + a SIMPLIFIED Phase 2 (reply round-trip) — skip the elaborate multi-staff Discord-account-linking/OAuth work entirely for now (that's explicitly deferred to when actual support staff join later). Since there's only one person who will ever reply from this Discord server, replies can be attributed to a single, configured Nxeon staff/admin user id (see "Reply attribution" below) rather than building a full identity-linking flow.

## Already done (do not redo)

A real Discord bot application exists and is already configured:
- `Setting` table already has these rows (read via `getSetting`/`getSettingBool` from `lib/settings.ts`, matching the exact pattern already used for `kb_bot_api_key` etc.):
  - `discord_application_id` (plain string)
  - `discord_public_key` (plain string, 64 hex chars — the Ed25519 public key for verifying interaction signatures)
  - `discord_bot_token` (ENCRYPTED via `lib/crypto-box.ts`'s `encryptSecret`/`decryptSecret` — same pattern as `kb_bot_api_key` in `lib/kb-llm.ts`'s `resolveBotKey()`, read that function for the exact decrypt-on-read pattern to copy)
  - `discord_guild_id` (plain string — the id of the one private Discord server this bridge posts into)
- The bot token is LIVE and verified working (confirmed via a direct `GET https://discord.com/api/v10/users/@me` call, bot username "Nxeon Support"). The guild is a real, currently-empty private Discord server called "Nxeon Cloud."
- Add one more setting yourself as part of this build: `discord_enabled` (a plain "true"/"false" kill-switch, matching the `registrar_namecheap_enabled`-style pattern in `lib/settings.ts` — default it to `"false"` so this ships dark until the owner flips it on after reviewing).
- Add one more setting: `discord_reply_as_user_id` (plain string, the Nxeon `User.id` that Discord-originated replies get attributed to as `TicketMessage.authorId`/chat equivalent). Leave it UNSET/empty by default — do not guess or hardcode a specific user id. Your code should treat a reply attempt as a clear, loud error (log it, and post a visible error back into the Discord thread: "⚠️ Discord replies aren't configured yet — set discord_reply_as_user_id in admin settings") if this setting is empty, rather than silently failing or attributing to a null/fake user. Report back clearly in your summary that this setting still needs a real value before replies will work, and that only I (the orchestrating session) or the owner should set it, since it needs the actual admin/owner Nxeon User.id.

## Codebase facts to ground your build (from the completed research — verified against actual file:line references, trust these)

- `Ticket`/`TicketMessage` models: `prisma/schema.prisma:278-299`. No `discordThreadId` field exists yet — add one (nullable String, additive).
- `ChatConversation`/`ChatMessage` models: `prisma/schema.prisma:2565-2602` (NOT "ChatSession" — that name doesn't exist). Add a nullable `discordThreadId` field to `ChatConversation` too.
- `lib/actions-support.ts`: `replyTicket` (lines ~87-149) does, inside `db.$transaction`: `ticketMessage.create` + `ticket.update({status: isStaff ? "ANSWERED" : "CUSTOMER_REPLY"})`, then OUTSIDE the transaction (best-effort, try/catch) a `notification.create` + `sendMail(emails.ticketReply(...))`. `createTicket` (line ~53) is the other ticket-creation entry point.
- **Tickets have a SECOND, independent writer**: the AI agent's `open_support_ticket` tool, executed by `openTicket()` in `lib/kb-tools.ts` (~lines 141-169) — this does NOT go through `createTicket` in actions-support.ts. Your Phase-1 mirror logic for "a new ticket was created" must fire from BOTH paths — the cleanest way is a single new shared helper both call, not duplicated relay logic.
- `lib/actions-chat.ts`: `replyToConversation` (~line 136) does `chatMessage.create` + `chatConversation.update({status:"OPEN", unreadForUser:true, assignedToId: staff.id})` in a transaction, then best-effort `notification.create`. `replyWithAttachment` (~line 190) is the attachment variant.
- Chat's customer-facing entry point is `/api/chat` (`app/api/chat/route.ts`) which calls `runAssistant` in `lib/kb-run.ts`. `lib/kb-run.ts:105-142`'s `escalate()` is where the AI currently emails ONE address (`kb_bot_agent_email` setting) when a human is explicitly requested — this is the ONLY existing human-handoff mechanism today. `lib/kb-run.ts:150`'s `checkEscalationTimeout()` handles the no-agent-available fallback after `kb_bot_window_sec` (default 180s).
- `app/api/stripe/webhook/route.ts` is the existing pattern to imitate for signature verification: reads raw body as text BEFORE any JSON parsing, verifies a signature header, returns 400/401 on failure, keeps the handler fast and idempotent (relies on a DB-level unique-constraint for idempotency, not on "we returned 200 so no retry").
- `lib/settings.ts` + `lib/actions-settings.ts` have the established encrypted-secret settings pattern (`type: "secret"` fields use `encryptSecret`/`decryptSecret` from `lib/crypto-box.ts`, AES-256-GCM keyed off `AUTH_SECRET`).
- `worker/index.ts` is the one existing long-running daemon (job-queue + periodic sweeps, `POLL_MS=3000`) — NOT needed for this build if you use the button+modal reply flow (see Discord platform facts below), but is the natural home later if plain-typed-message replies are ever wanted instead.

## Discord platform facts (from the completed research — verified against current 2026 Discord docs, trust these, do not re-verify from scratch)

- **Forum channels cannot have private threads** — only plain text channels support private threads. Since this is a single-person-only, fully-private guild (only the owner + this bot are members), just use a **plain text channel-per-ticket/conversation** (or a forum channel with PUBLIC threads is also fine here since there's no second party to hide anything from within this one guild) — your call, but justify it in your report.
- **HTTP-only bot, no persistent Gateway connection needed.** Build this as: (a) a Next.js API route acting as the Discord "Interactions Endpoint" for button clicks + modal submissions (signed, Ed25519-verified), and (b) plain REST calls (`https://discord.com/api/v10/...`) triggered from Nxeon's own server-side code to create channels/threads and post messages. Do NOT build a discord.js Gateway client or any new long-running process — that's explicitly the wrong approach here per the completed research, given this codebase's existing poll/request-response architecture.
- **Ed25519 signature verification is mandatory** for the Interactions Endpoint. Every interaction POST carries `X-Signature-Ed25519` and `X-Signature-Timestamp` headers; verify by checking the signature against `timestamp + rawBody` using the stored `discord_public_key`. Use Node's built-in `crypto.verify` with the `'ed25519'` algorithm (Node 20+ supports this natively via `crypto.verify(null, Buffer.concat([Buffer.from(timestamp), rawBody]), { key: publicKeyObject, ... })` — look up the exact current Node.js API for Ed25519 verification with a raw hex public key; you may need `crypto.createPublicKey` with the raw key wrapped in an appropriate DER/SPKI header, or use a small, well-known verification snippet — many Discord bot frameworks publish the exact ~15-line Node crypto snippet for this, get it right, this is genuinely security-critical). Return `401` on any verification failure. You MUST handle Discord's `PING` interaction type (type 1) by responding with `{type: 1}` (PONG) — Discord will not save the endpoint URL in the Developer Portal otherwise, and will periodically re-send PINGs and deliberately-invalid signatures to test the endpoint.
- Discord REST basics you'll need: `POST /guilds/{guild.id}/channels` (create a channel), `POST /channels/{channel.id}/messages` (post a message, supports `components` for buttons), `POST /channels/{channel.id}/threads` (create a thread), `PATCH /webhooks/{application.id}/{interaction.token}/messages/@original` or the interaction response mechanism for responding to a button click, `POST /interactions/{interaction.id}/{interaction.token}/callback` for responding to an interaction (e.g. type 9 `MODAL` to open a modal in response to a button click, or type 4 `CHANNEL_MESSAGE_WITH_SOURCE` for a simple ack). Auth header for bot REST calls: `Authorization: Bot <token>`.
- Discord's Components v2 message components: a button is `{type: 2, style: 1, label: "Reply", custom_id: "reply:<ticketId>"}` inside an action row `{type: 1, components: [...]}`. A modal response has `{type: 9, data: {custom_id: "reply_modal:<ticketId>", title: "Reply to customer", components: [{type: 1, components: [{type: 4, custom_id: "reply_text", style: 2, label: "Your reply", required: true}]}]}}` (type 4 = TEXT_INPUT, style 2 = paragraph/multiline). On modal submit (interaction type 5, `MODAL_SUBMIT`), the submitted text is in `interaction.data.components[0].components[0].value`.
- Rate limits are generous (50 req/s global) and not a practical concern at this volume — don't over-engineer rate-limit handling, just don't ignore a 429 response (respect `Retry-After` if you ever hit one, simple retry-once is enough).

## What to build

1. **Schema**: add `discordThreadId String?` to `Ticket` and to `ChatConversation` (additive, nullable — no migration data-loss risk). Since this worktree shares a symlinked `node_modules` with the LIVE production app, follow the EXACT same discipline the Namecheap-integration work used earlier this session: do NOT run `npx prisma generate` or `npx prisma db push` from this worktree (that would regenerate the SHARED Prisma Client against a schema not yet live in the real DB, breaking the running production app). Write the schema field, but read/write it via `(row as any).discordThreadId` casts until a human runs `prisma db push` + `generate` for real as part of promoting this branch — document this exact hazard in a comment on the new fields, matching how `Domain.renewPriceCents` was documented in the Namecheap work.

2. **A small `lib/discord.ts` module**: bot REST client (auth header, base URL, a `discordFetch()` helper), Ed25519 interaction-signature verification, and small typed helpers for "create a channel," "post a message with a Reply button," "open a modal," "read a modal submission." Read config via `getSetting`/`getSettingBool`/`decryptSecret` — never a bare `process.env.DISCORD_*` (though a `process.env.DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` fallback mirroring `resolveBotKey()`'s pattern in `lib/kb-llm.ts` is fine as a secondary fallback, matching that established convention).

3. **The mirror (Phase 1)**: a function that, given a ticket or chat-conversation id, creates a Discord channel (if `discordThreadId` is null) named descriptively (e.g. `ticket-<shortid>` or using the customer's name), posts the opening message with real customer/context (name, email, plan — you can query the same data the AI agent's `get_account_overview`-style tools use, or just the `User` row directly, whichever is simpler for a single message), and includes a "Reply" button. Save the returned channel/thread id back onto the row. Wire this into: `createTicket` (actions-support.ts), `openTicket` (kb-tools.ts), and the chat entry point (wherever a NEW `ChatConversation` first gets a message — find the exact right hook point by reading `runAssistant`/`app/api/chat/route.ts`). For an EXISTING ticket/conversation that already has a `discordThreadId`, just post the new message into the existing channel instead of creating a new one.

4. **The reply round-trip (simplified Phase 2)**: a new webhook route, likely `app/api/webhooks/discord/route.ts`, handling: PING (respond PONG), the Reply button click (respond with a MODAL), and MODAL_SUBMIT (extract the reply text, then call a shared internal reply-writing function). This means refactoring `replyTicket`/`replyToConversation` — extract their core DB-write logic (message create + status update + notification + email) into plain, non-"use server" functions the existing server actions AND this new webhook route can both call, so there is exactly ONE reply-writing code path regardless of which surface (Discord, `/admin/support`, `/admin/chat`) originated it. Be careful: these are live, currently-working, RBAC-relevant files — `lib/actions-support.ts`'s own top-of-file comment describes a PREVIOUS real RBAC bug in this exact file, so refactor surgically (extract logic, don't rewrite behavior) and make sure the existing "use server" actions still do their own auth check (`requireTicketActor()` etc.) before calling the shared core — the shared core itself should NOT re-check auth (the webhook path's "auth" is Discord's own signature verification + the fact that only the configured `discord_reply_as_user_id` can ever be attributed, which is the deliberate simplification for personal-use).

5. Determine WHICH Nxeon user a Discord reply is attributed to via the `discord_reply_as_user_id` setting described above (empty by default, loud error if unset when someone tries to reply).

## Constraints

- Read `lib/kb-run.ts` in full before touching anything chat-related — do not let a Discord-mirrored ticket/conversation confuse the AI agent's own state machine (e.g. don't let your mirror code accidentally look like a "human reply" that would silence the bot, unless a human genuinely did reply via Discord, in which case that IS correct behavior).
- Every new customer-PII-bearing Discord message should avoid posting anything payment-adjacent (no raw card data — none of this ever reaches app-layer code anyway per this platform's Stripe/PayPal/Coinbase integration, so this should be a non-issue, just don't go out of your way to surface anything sensitive beyond name/email/plan/service-id).
- `discord_enabled` (the kill-switch) must actually gate everything — when `false`, the mirror functions become silent no-ops (never throw, never block the real ticket/chat flow — a Discord outage or misconfiguration must NEVER break a customer's ability to open a ticket or chat), matching this codebase's established "third-party integration is always best-effort, wrapped in try/catch, non-blocking" pattern (see how `sendMail` failures are handled in `replyTicket`).

## Test baseline

`npm test` currently has 34 pre-existing, unrelated failures (pricing/proration/auth-baseline tests) — established, known baseline. Confirm zero NEW failures beyond that same set of 34.

## Verification

1. `npx tsc --noEmit` — must be clean.
2. `npm test` — compare against the 34-failure baseline, confirm zero new failures. Add real tests for: the Ed25519 signature verification logic (valid signature accepted, invalid rejected, PING handled) — this is security-critical code and must be genuinely tested, not just eyeballed.
3. **A real, live smoke test is appropriate and encouraged here** since you have real working credentials and a real (currently empty) Discord server: write a small one-off script that calls your `lib/discord.ts` helpers directly to create ONE test channel in the real guild and post ONE test message with a Reply button, confirm it appears via the Discord REST API (`GET` the channel back), then DELETE that test channel afterward so the guild is left clean for the owner. Do NOT leave test artifacts sitting in the real Discord server. Do not attempt to test the full webhook/modal round-trip live (that requires Discord to actually call back your endpoint, which needs a public URL — not testable from this sandboxed worktree; cover that path with the signature-verification unit tests instead and note in your report that the full round-trip needs a real deployment with a public webhook URL registered in the Discord Developer Portal before it can be end-to-end tested).

## Report back

Summarize exactly what you built, the schema fields added (and the explicit "not yet pushed to DB" caveat), how you scoped the channel-vs-thread decision, confirmation of all verification steps including the live smoke-test result, exactly what still needs to happen before this can go live (the `discord_reply_as_user_id` setting needs a real value; `prisma db push`+`generate` needs to run for real; `discord_enabled` needs to flip to true; the Interactions Endpoint URL needs to be registered in Discord's Developer Portal once this is deployed somewhere with a public URL, since Discord requires a live, PING-answering URL before it will save it). Leave the change uncommitted in the worktree for review.

/**
 * Shared source-reading helpers for the structural tripwire suites.
 *
 * NOT named `*.test.ts` on purpose: `npm test` globs `test/*.test.ts`, so this
 * module is imported, never executed as a suite. It used to live inside
 * customer-actions-guards.test.ts and be imported from there, which made every
 * assertion in that file run a second time under the importing suite's name.
 */

/**
 * Blank out the CONTENTS of every string / template literal, on top of
 * `stripComments`. Quotes and backticks are kept so the token stream still
 * parses by eye; only what is between them is erased.
 *
 * `${…}` interpolations inside a template literal are KEPT, because they are
 * executable code, not string content. Erasing them would hide exactly the
 * detail some tripwires exist to check — a rate-limit bucket keyed on
 * `` `x:${user.id}` `` versus one keyed on `` `x:${clientIp}` `` is the
 * difference between limiting an account and limiting a forgeable header, and
 * both collapse to the same blank if the interpolation goes with the text.
 *
 * WHY BOTH ARE NEEDED. `stripComments` deliberately preserves literals (there is
 * a test asserting exactly that), because plenty of tripwires need to read a
 * literal — "is MAIL_HOST still `mail.nxeon.cloud`?". But a tripwire asserting a
 * CALL is present must not match a mention of that call inside a string, and
 * this repo is full of such mentions: error copy, audit-log `action` values, and
 * doc strings that quote the very function being checked. Comments alone are not
 * enough here — `"Couldn't apply forwarding on the mail server"` and
 * `detail: "mailbox.suspend"` are executable code, and a naive grep is happy
 * with either.

## Summary

Built the Discord support bridge in `/opt/nxeon-wip-discord-bridge` (branch `feature/discord-support-bridge`), uncommitted, per scope.

**New files:**
- `lib/discord.ts` — REST client (`discordFetch`, bot-token/guild/app-id/public-key getters via `getSetting`/`decryptSecret`), Ed25519 interaction-signature verification (`verifyDiscordSignature`, built from Node's native `crypto.createPublicKey`/`verify` by reconstructing an SPKI DER key from Discord's raw 32-byte hex key — no `tweetnacl` dependency added), and typed helpers (`createGuildTextChannel`, `postChannelMessage`, `getChannel`, `deleteChannel`, modal/interaction-response builders).
- `lib/discord-bridge.ts` — the mirror + reply logic: `mirrorNewTicketToDiscord`, `mirrorTicketReplyToDiscord`, `mirrorChatMessageToDiscord` (create-channel-or-post-to-existing, all `discord_enabled`-gated and fully try/caught), plus `submitDiscordReply` for the reply round-trip and the `dc_reply:*`/`dc_reply_modal:*` custom-id scheme.
- `lib/reply-core.ts` — `writeTicketReply`/`writeChatReply`, the DB-write bodies extracted **verbatim** from `replyTicket`/`replyToConversation` so there is exactly one reply-writing path for dashboard, admin, and Discord. No auth inside — callers (including the "use server" actions) still do their own check first, exactly as before.
- `app/api/webhooks/discord/route.ts` — the Interactions Endpoint: reads raw body before parsing (mirrors the Stripe webhook pattern), verifies Ed25519 before trusting anything, handles PING/button-click(→modal)/modal-submit.
- `test/discord-signature.test.ts` — 11 new tests: real-keypair signature verification (valid accepted, tampered body/timestamp/wrong-key/garbage-probe/malformed-hex all rejected, never throws) plus structural checks that the webhook reads raw-before-parse, verifies-before-parse, 401s on bad signatures, and answers PING correctly.

**Modified:** `prisma/schema.prisma` (added `Ticket.discordThreadId` / `ChatConversation.discordThreadId`, both nullable, with the same "NOT YET PUSHED" caveat comment style as `Domain.renewPriceCents`), `lib/settings.ts` (added `discord_application_id/public_key/bot_token/guild_id/enabled/reply_as_user_id`, `discord_bot_token` added to `SECRET_KEYS`), `lib/actions-support.ts`, `lib/actions-chat.ts`, `lib/kb-tools.ts`, `app/api/chat/route.ts`, `app/api/chat/upload/route.ts` (mirror hooks wired into ticket/chat creation and replies).

**Design calls:** plain text channel per ticket/conversation (not forum threads — forum channels can't have private threads, and this whole guild is single-member private anyway); no discord.js Gateway client, pure REST + one webhook route, matching the codebase's poll/request-response shape.

**Verification:**
- `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean.
- `npm test` — 1294 tests, 34 failures, **identical to the pre-existing baseline list** (confirmed by diffing against the same suite run with all Discord changes stashed). Zero new failures.

This needs a human with "Manage Server" on the "Nxeon Cloud" guild to authorize the bot via: `https://discord.com/oauth2/authorize?client_id=1543447833221398528&permissions=85008&scope=bot` (permissions = VIEW_CHANNEL + MANAGE_CHANNELS + SEND_MESSAGES + EMBED_LINKS + READ_MESSAGE_HISTORY). I left a ready-to-run smoke-test script at `/tmp/claude-0/-root/4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc/scratchpad/smoke_discord.mts` (creates one channel + message + button, verifies via GET, deletes it) for whoever completes that invite step.
